review.algorithm_assessment: The count G_n of simple noncrossing graphs on n cyclically ordered labeled vertices is 2^(n-1) times the large Schroeder number R_(n-2), for n>=2. Boundary edges are independently optional. A required edge at cyclic distance d splits the polygon into d+1 and n-d+1 vertices; choosing graphs on the two sides with their common boundary edge fixed present gives G_(d+1)*G_(n-d+1)/4 graphs. Linearity of expectation reduces the weighted answer to a sum over d of this probability times sum_i a_i*a_(i+d). Compute all such correlations by exact packed integer convolution, with byte lanes large enough for n*max(a)^2 so carries cannot corrupt coefficients. Compute Schroeder numbers with (r+1)R_r=3(2r-1)R_(r-1)-(r-2)R_(r-2), then divide by 4*G_n modulo the prime. The n=2 case is covered directly by G_2=2.
